cells.place: Do. No. 2.
cells.remarks: Records the endowment made by various mahājanangal including the peasants of different ūrs for the midnight worship of god Śrī Tējinvēśvarasvāmi of Tiruvili molalai in Rājagambhīravalanāḍu. The endowment was made in terms of magamai from the kuḍivāram paddy. It is also stated that the rates of the usages is four nāḷ per hundred kalam of paddy to be collected to the temple as kūlippichchai.

cells.remarks: Records the gift of a village for providing a feeding charity. The gift was made by Vijayaraghunātharāya Toṇḍaimāṉ, son of Tirumalaippa Toṇḍaimāṉ, one of the Kāṇi udaiya araiya-makkaḷ residing at Alumbil in Paṇri-sūla-nāḍu a sub-division of Rājarāja-vaḷanāḍu.

cells.place: Kōdūru. - Pillar lying on the tank bund of the village.
cells.remarks: Registers the gift of the village Kōrūr along with the open field and waste lands to Brahmaliṅgabhaṭṭa belonging to Gaṅgēśvara of Poṭlakere by Mahāsāmanta Gaṅgayyarasa when the king was camping at a place called Rāvula-kōṇe. The grant was made in front of god Rāmēśvara of Pōlapaṛela. The inscription is installed by Bittiyya of Gaṅgarasa's family. (Published: Journal of Epigraphical Society of India, Vol. XVIII, pp. 118ff.).

cells.remarks: Records the installation of the deity Ramaramaṇa at the place called Baudhām situated on the bank of the river Kṛishṇā by mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Kandūri Toṇḍaya-chōḍa, whom is described as Kōdūri-puravaradhīśvarāshīvara and belonging to Kāśyapa-gōtra and Karikālānvaya. While he was ruling from his capital Pānugallur over Kandūru-nāḍu sub-division and Koṇḍapalli-nāḍu, his minister Gōpati son of Mēdama granted two khaṇḍugas of land and taxes (surikas) for maintaining perpetual lamp to the above deity.

cells.place:
Āgamōtūkūru. - A square pillar
standing in front of the
Añjanēya temple.
cells.date:
Śaka 1204,
Chitrabhānu Vaiśākha
śu. 7, Thursday =
1282 A.D., April 16
cells.remarks: Records the consecration of the god Vīramanāthadēva and gifts of lands (details given) and Dēvarājya-mādas by mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Rāmanātha-dēva chōḍa of Kandūri family for the aṅga-ranga-bhōga and other services of the above deity. The gift is stated to have been made for his own merit and for the merit of his father. Further it also records the gift of lands made from Śrīpārvata on Thursday the 14th of the dark fortnight in the month of Māgha in the cyclic year Pramādīcha (1314 A.D., February 14). [Published in Sāsana-Saṅpuṭi (Telugu), pp. 171 ff].

cells.date: Bhūlōkamalla year [3*], Sādhāraṇa, Āśvayuja, Sunday, Solar eclipse = 1130 A.D., October 5. The eclipse occurred on Saturday when the month of Āśvayuja ended
cells.remarks: States that Ambāhanthāda Daṇḍanāyaka, the vaḍḍarāvula-suṁkādhikāri of Kibbeṭaya gave two suṁkas as compensation (parihāra) for every thirty perukas of salt received from agāra every year for the anga-bhōga of the deity Kēśavadēva. Also two suṁkas for the perudas from outside as well as a rīka per month from the suṁka was given as compensation for maintaining the lamp to the same deity, installed by Yajñavalki Kēśava-bhaṭṭa (Do. p. 12).

cells.date: Śaka 1181 Siddhārthi Māgha, ba. 14, Thursday, = 1260 A.D., February 12 Thursday. The tithi ended on the previous day.
cells.remarks: Gives the genealogy of the king commencing from Bhillama. Records the grant of lands at Pērūru to the god Svayambhū-Sōmēśvara and to the minor deities (Parivāra-dēvatas) for the various food offerings made during the morning, afternoon and night services. Also records the various produces assigned for the food-offerings made during the afternoon service to the deities Kalakēśvara, Dhārēśvara and Mailēśvara. It also registers the gift of lands made to the deity Kēśavadēva installed by Yājñavalka Kēśavabhaṭṭa. The provision made for the food offerings to Vināyaka and Kēśavadēva is enumerated in detail. The king is also stated to have granted lands in the dominion of Kākatiya Gaṇapati to the various brāhmaṇas (Do. No. 12, p. 14).

cells.date:

Puṣya śu. 3,
Uttarāyaṇa saṅkrānti
Sunday = 1082 A.D.,
December 25.
cells.remarks: Built in. Records the gift of land and house sites by mahāmamaṇḍalēśvara Kākatīya Bētarasa to Vīr[a][k]amala Jinaalaya built by mahāmamaṇḍalēśvara Mēdarasa of Uravāḍi a subordinate of Tribhuvanamalla Vikramāditya (VI). The later was stated to have belonged to Veṅgoṇḍa-kula and the family of Mādhavavarma who was described as a possessor 8000 elephants, 10 crores of horses and countless foot-soldiers. The inscription was written by Āryapayya and Śrīdhara (Published in Inscription of Andhra Pradesh, Warangal District, No. 14, pp. 26 ff.).

cells.remarks: States that during the time of Mīr Jumla, Khān-i-A'zam Dilāwar Khān, the boundary of the village Arak was fixed by the Dīwān-i-Ḥadd (i.e. Surveyor General) at the instance of the reigning king. The officers present were Bilāl Khān, the ḥawāladār, Sayyid Maḥmūd, the Na'īb-i-Ghaibat (In Minister in Absence) of the mu'āmala (district) of Mubārakābād (i.e. Miraj), Malik Raiḥān, the Salāhdār (armour-bearer) and Sharza Khān, the Muqaddar (i.e. fief-holder) of the village Arak, Sayyid Nūru'd-Dīn, Mahāldār of the royal court and Manṣūr Khān, the Sarbarāh of the village Arak. Ends with an imprecation against the violators.

cells.location: BABERU TAHSIL Kamāsīn.
cells.place: Do. Grave of Mr. John Wanchope. On a marble slab.
cells.remarks: Reads: (1) Sacred to the Memory (2) of (3) JOHN WANCHOPE ESQUIRE (4) OF NIDDRIE NEAR EDINBURGH (5) Collector of BUNDELKHUND in 1809 & 1810 A.D. (6) and Judge of BUNDELKHUND in 1818 A.D. (7) He successfully exerted (8) himself to gain affections, (9) and promote the happiness (10) of those over whom he was (11) placed and supported by his (12) personal conduct and char (13) acter the honour and interests (14) of Governments by whom his (15) valuable services have been (16) frequently and most honourably (17) acknowledged. Mr. WANCHÕPE (18) was of the ancient family of (19) NEDDERY near EDINBURGH, and (20) he departed this life at KA (21) LINGAR on the 12th August 1818 (22) in the 36th year of his age. (23) CALCUTTA BROWN & CO SCTS. States that this is the grave of Muhammad Anwar Khān, Police Inspector, Retired, who died on the given date. Written by 'Abdu'r Raḥmān.
